s1.syndrome_frame: A firm mass in the breast with possible fixation to underlying muscle, in a patient with a history of breast cancer
salient_findings: 20 mm firm mass fixed to the pectoralis major muscle
Focal asymmetrical density in the retromammary space on mammography
Lobulated, well-defined mass with heterogeneous internal echoes on ultrasonography
key_facts: 59-year-old woman
Lump in the lower outer quadrant of her left breast
History of breast-conserving surgery, endocrine therapy, and radiation to the left breast
Previous carcinoma in the upper inner quadrant of the left breast
20 mm firm mass fixed to the pectoralis major muscle
Overlying skin uninvolved
No palpable axillary lymph nodes
Mammography showed a focal asymmetrical density in the retromammary space
Ultrasonography revealed a lobulated, well-defined mass
Core-needle biopsy suggested atrophic mammary glands
Lesion increased in size on three-month follow-up

shortlist.label: Locoregional breast cancer recurrence
shortlist.why_kept: History of breast cancer and new firm mass fixed to underlying muscle

shortlist.label: Phyllodes tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Lobulated, well-defined mass with heterogeneous internal echoes on ultrasonography

shortlist.label: Sarcoma of the breast
shortlist.why_kept: Firm mass fixed to pectoralis major muscle and history of radiation therapy

shortlist.label: Fibromatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Firm mass fixed to underlying muscle and history of breast cancer

shortlist.label: Radiation-induced fibrosis
shortlist.why_kept: History of radiation therapy to the left breast and new firm mass

raw.rationale: History of breast-conserving surgery, endocrine therapy, and radiation to the left breast, combined with a new lump and increasing size of the lesion, suggests a recurrence of breast cancer.

rejected.label: Phyllodes tumor
rejected.why: While possible, the history of previous breast cancer and radiation therapy makes recurrence more likely

rejected.label: Sarcoma of the breast
rejected.why: Less common than breast cancer recurrence in this context

rejected.label: Fibromatosis
rejected.why: Typically presents as a rapidly growing mass, but the history of breast cancer and radiation makes recurrence more likely

rejected.label: Radiation-induced fibrosis
rejected.why: Would not typically present as a discrete, growing mass
